predecessors.name: Twenty-sixth Dynasty of Egypt
predecessors.text: Egypt as the Saite kings held it, conquered by Cambyses II at Pelusium in May 525

successors.name: Twenty-eighth Dynasty of Egypt
successors.text: Egypt, from which Amyrtaeus expelled the Persians (Memphis in 405, kingship in 404)

ledger.x: 525: Cambyses II wins Egypt at Pelusium and the Twenty-seventh Dynasty begins.
525: Egypt is held by the Persian kings as the First Egyptian Satrapy (525-404).
460: Inaros II raises the western Delta.
460: the Persian army, led by the satrap Achaemenes, is defeated and the Persians fall back on the Memphis citadel.
454: the western Delta returns to Persian rule after Inaros is defeated and taken to Susa.
405: Amyrtaeus expels the Persians from Memphis.
404: the Persian war for Egypt ends in an Egyptian success; Amyrtaeus proclaims himself Pharaoh after Darius II's death.
404: the Twenty-seventh Dynasty ends with the rebellion of Amyrtaeus.

wars.name: Battle of Pelusium (525 BC)
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Cambyses II took Memphis, captured Psamtik III and became pharaoh; the Libyans made a truce.

wars.name: Revolt of Petubastis III
wars.outcome: A native prince rebelled in late 522 or early 521 and Darius reportedly ended the revolt; no territory is described.

wars.name: Revolt of Inaros II
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Megabyzus besieged the Athenians on Prosopitis for eighteen months, retook the Delta and took Inaros to Susa.

wars.name: Revolt of Amyrtaeus
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: the Persians were expelled from Memphis in 405 and Amyrtaeus declared himself pharaoh in 404.

certainty.note: The pages give no borders for the satrapy; only Egypt as a whole is named.
